source.title: Knowledge Distillation with Noisy Labels for Natural Language Understanding
source.authors: Shivendra Bhardwaj; Abbas Ghaddar; Ahmad Rashid; Khalil Bibi; Cheng-Yang Li; A. Ghodsi; P. Langlais; Mehdi Rezagholizadeh

record.tranche_reason: Tests label-noise effects in NLU knowledge distillation, an extension of the claim's noisy-label setting to language tasks and distilled models.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates noisy labels on GLUE dev sets and reports that Vanilla KD training loss decreases by overfitting noisy labels. It does not report training error on completely random labels, chance test error, or results at 100% noise.
record.test_reason: Label refinement uses the premise that clean examples have smaller losses early in training. The study evaluates noise mitigation through GLUE dev performance, without measuring perfect training-set fitting or the temporal ordering of clean-label learning and noise memorization. Declining training loss alone does not establish those effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: noisy labels substantially harm NLU knowledge distillation; Co-Distill and label refinement improve robustness, but the problem remains challenging.
record.recipe_differences: Uses GLUE text classification tasks, BERT-base as teacher, distillBERT students, and knowledge distillation under 25% and 50% label noise; it does not reproduce the original image-labeling experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise level (0%, 25%, 50%) and training method affect GLUE dev performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports decreasing GLUE dev performance at 0%, 25%, and 50% label noise. BERT-base averages are 83.2, 73.9, and 58.1; Vanilla KD averages are 81.8, 73.0, and 57.2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing artificial label noise degrades held-out NLU performance for pretrained teachers and distilled students under the tested training procedures.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.4 says Vanilla KD training loss continues decreasing while dev loss flattens, attributing this to overfitting noisy labels. No training-error values or separate clean/noisy learning curves are supplied.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vanilla KD can continue reducing its training objective without improving held-out loss under 50% label noise.

record.problems: No training-error or chance-test-error measurements are reported for the claim's behavior. Noise is tested only at 25% and 50%, and the authors state they do not evaluate beyond 50%. Results are averages over 3 random seeds, but uncertainty intervals are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows retained: the reported dev-set performance and qualitative training-loss observations do not measure the fitting of completely random labels or the full training-error and test-error behavior required by the versions.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels to zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged training hyperparameters.
Relative training time for real and random labels and convergence time across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training-set fitting throughout increasing corruption and the joint trajectory of training error and test error toward chance. Dev performance at 0%, 25%, and 50% noise establishes degradation only.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing it harms clean-label generalization.
Direct comparison over training of shared-pattern learning and subsequent memorization of noisy labels; this ordering is assumed from prior work.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 tested designation is too strong: held-out degradation does not establish the version's coupled perfect-fitting and generalization behavior. Omitted dev scores and qualitative loss observations are already declared in rows_left_out. Image inputs are not a requirement of V1.

versions.untested_parts: Image labels, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters are not tested.
Training time to fit random versus true labels, and convergence time across corruption fractions, are not reported.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.

The study tests 0%, 25%, and 50% noisy labels and reports dev performance decline and qualitative training-loss behavior, but does not report perfect training error or test error at chance; it does not test noise levels above 50%.
Weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, and their removal are not tested.
The study does not compare learning patterns shared by clean data with memorization of noisy or random labels over training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
